key_insight: For gradient descent on smooth Polyak–Łojasiewicz functions, multi-step SDP analysis improves on repeated one-step bounds when √3/L < t < 2/L, revealing an initial transient followed by eventual geometric decay.
engineering_relevance: The results sharpen convergence guarantees for constant-step gradient descent under smoothness and Polyak–Łojasiewicz assumptions, especially at larger stable step sizes.
method: Formulate N-step objective-gap bounds as an SDP using pairwise smoothness and pointwise Polyak–Łojasiewicz constraints.
Solve a reduced SDP with consecutive-pair constraints analytically across three step-size regimes.
Certify bounds with explicit primal and dual feasible solutions.
evidence_signal: Numerical SDP experiments guided the analytic certificates; the reduced and full SDPs match for 0 < t ≤ √3/L, while the improved asymptotic factor is tight for the full SDP when √3/L < t < 2/L.
watch_item: These are certified SDP upper bounds, not established exact worst-case rates over smooth Polyak–Łojasiewicz functions, because an exact interpolation condition is unavailable.
paper_title: Multi-Step Performance Estimation for Gradient Descent under the Polyak Lojasiewicz Condition
